scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a timber loft, a concrete tower and a restaurant. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: Building approval and certificate of insurance
Most managed buildings won't schedule work until they have both, and some name specific insurance limits.
Booked time windows decide when materials and crews get in, and how long a day on site really is.
Most West Loop streets have little parking near the door, so carrying tools and materials in takes time.
Wire can be fished through wood framing, has to run in conduit across concrete, or needs approved core drilling through a slab.
In a loft, conduit is part of the look. It's planned so it reads as intentional, which takes longer than hidden wiring.
Heavy chandeliers on 14-foot-plus ceilings need the right support, the right box and sometimes a lift.
Restaurants and occupied offices often need early, late or weekend work, so agree the hours before the job is scheduled.
In high-rises, fire alarm and life-safety tie-ins go through the building's own contractor.
Many unit jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Build-outs need plans and a standard review.
Boards often want a written proposal before they approve work in common areas or shared garages.
Whose meter the charger runs from, the building's spare capacity, and submetering decide the design.
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a West Loop job depend on the factors below. A fixture swap in a walk-up and the same fixture on a 16-foot loft ceiling aren't the same job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosing_building_why: A loft with an exposed timber ceiling, a concrete-slab tower and a restaurant kitchen are three different jobs.
choosing_building_answer: High-rise and loft units, new-construction mid-rises, tenant build-outs and a Halsted St restaurant
choosing_paperwork_why: Most towers want a certificate of insurance, and sometimes an elevator booking, before work is scheduled.
where_we_fit: Highlights is a family-owned contractor. In the West Loop we're the right call for condo, loft and townhome work, lighting, panels, EV chargers, restaurants, tenant build-outs and mid-rise new construction. Base-building work on a 40-storey tower is a job for the large commercial firms, and we'll tell you so.

honest_context: We're a north-side shop. Most of our 1,213 Chicago permits are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and the 27th covers part of the West Loop. Our West Loop work peaked with the mid-rise building wave of 2013 to 2020. Since then it has been mostly unit-level work: lighting, panels, circuits and EV chargers.
The busiest names in West Loop permits are large commercial contractors working on towers and office floors. That's a different job from yours if you're refitting a loft.

faq: Do you work in West Loop high-rise buildings?

Yes. We work to the building's rules: a certificate of insurance before scheduling, booked freight elevator time, approved working hours and the building engineer's sign-off where it's needed. Reviewers describe our crews handling high-rise parking, elevators and building rules without fuss.
Can you install an EV charger in my condo building's garage?

Usually, yes. The design depends on whose electrical service the charger runs from, the building's spare capacity, whether the association wants a submeter, and its approval process. We provide the certificate of insurance and a proposal the association can review.
Do I need a permit for electrical work in my West Loop condo?

Most electrical work in Chicago needs a permit, and many unit jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Our own West Loop record includes permitted lighting work in condo units. We tell you at the walkthrough whether your job needs one, and we pull and close it.
Do you work on restaurants on Randolph Street and in Greektown?
Yes: kitchen equipment circuits, service upgrades, lighting, emergency and exit lighting, and signage, scheduled around service. Our West Loop record includes a restaurant build-out on S Halsted.
Which West Loop ZIP codes do you cover?
All of them: 60607, 60661 and the part of 60606 west of the river, along with every other Chicago neighbourhood.
